name: Harris
desc:
Patient Account Representative |  $17 - $24/hr | Data Entry and Phone, Billing/Claims Focus
Company: Harris Computer (healthcare business unit)
Industry: Healthcare | Patient Billing & Accounts Receivable
What Your Day Will Look Like:
 This role has you managing a work queue of patient accounts, chasing down accurate and timely payment on claims that haven't gone smoothly. You're checking billing data for accuracy, fixing errors, and reading through denied claims to figure out why they were rejected so you can either resubmit or file an appeal.
A meaningful part of the job is reviewing aging accounts, ones that have been sitting unpaid for a while, and either working to collect what's owed or escalating to formal collections when needed, following established guidelines either way. You're also documenting everything thoroughly, verifying that payments received actually match what was contractually owed, and catching things like non-covered or out-of-network charges that need adjusting.
There's a phone component too, you'll be taking calls from patients with billing questions, and sometimes calling patients directly to get or share account information. So this blends real research/investigative billing work with some direct patient communication.
assessment: Expect an assessment on typing, simulations on using multiple systems, records keeping, and basic office software
skills:
Actual Minimum Requirements
Education Minimum: Not specified in posting.
 Required Experience: Not specified by years in this posting, though similar Harris Computer/healthcare billing postings commonly ask for prior medical billing or patient account experience.
 Preferred Experience: Prior experience in business office, patient billing, or collections/reimbursement procedures in a healthcare setting.
 Required Skills:
Ability to interpret and resolve denied claims
Strong attention to detail for billing data accuracy
Comfort with collections and escalation procedures
Professional phone communication with patients
Ability to maintain confidentiality of patient health information
Strong documentation habits
Best Fit
This role is ideal for:
Someone with prior medical billing, patient accounts, or healthcare collections experience
Participants who are comfortable blending detail-heavy claims research with some direct patient phone contact
Anyone who enjoys problem-solving around why a claim was denied and how to fix it
People who can handle collections-adjacent conversations professionally when accounts are past due
Not a Good Fit for:
Participants without any medical billing or healthcare administrative background
Someone who wants a purely phone-based role without claims research and documentation work
Anyone uncomfortable with the collections/escalation piece of the job
Top 10 Resume Keywords:
Patient account management
Medical billing
Claims denial resolution
Accounts receivable
Collections
Insurance verification
HIPAA compliance
Healthcare reimbursement
Aging account review
Patient communication
notes:
Expected Application & Interviewing Process:
Application
Expect an assessment at the end of the application or directly emailed to you.
If assessment is passing, expect a recruiter to reach out via email or text for a phone screen.
If phone screen passes you can expect the final interview.
 Total time to hire from date of application can be anywhere from 3-15 days on average.
4-5 interview questions for this role:
Tell me about your experience resolving a denied insurance claim, from identifying the issue to resubmitting or appealing.
How do you approach a collections conversation with a patient about a past-due balance?
Describe your experience reviewing billing data for accuracy and catching errors.
How do you stay organized managing a work queue of multiple accounts at different stages?
How do you handle a patient who's upset or confused about their bill?
